answer: Each identity claims one ridge parcel on an island registry and locks a 70-credit bond. It publishes a cipher commitment binding its work to that parcel; an auditor recomputes it against the deed registry and rejects a second opening on the parcel. Fees rise on a ridge: the k-th parcel costs 30+2(k-1) credits, so the 1,000th costs 2,028 and 1,000 fakes pay 1,029,000 in fees plus 70,000 locked bonds. A parcel-rental ring fails because a rented deed's cipher opening does not match its owner key, so both bonds burn. An honest identity pays 30 once and recovers its 70 bond after a clean epoch.
